The goal of this notebook is to quantify the impact of nutrient enrichment on
the presence of fish species in rivers, as done for large dams in
[D12](D12-dam-impact-presence.qmd). To do so, we need to

- get the river nutrient measurements from NAIADES
- match the nutrient measurements to the fish sampling visits (space and time)
- model the effect of nutrients on the presence of each species

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
devtools::load_all()
nice_theme()
```

## Nutrient data

### Presentation

The chemical measurements of rivers come from the NAIADES database,
downloaded with the Hub'Eau API (target `naiades_pc`). We focus on 9 parameters:

- **ammonium** (NH₄⁺): reduced nitrogen, mostly from wastewater and
manure; toxic to fish in its un-ionised form (NH₃) at high pH and temperature
- **nitrite** (NO₂⁻): intermediate of the oxidation of ammonium into nitrate,
toxic to fish at low concentrations
- **nitrate** (NO₃⁻): oxidised nitrogen, mostly from agricultural leaching
- **Kjeldahl nitrogen** (NKj): organic nitrogen plus ammonium
- **orthophosphate** (PO₄³⁻): dissolved phosphorus directly available to algae
- **total phosphorus** (Ptot): dissolved and particulate phosphorus,
expressed as P
- **temperature** (°C)
- **dissolved oxygen** (O₂, mg/L)
- **oxygen saturation** (%): dissolved oxygen relative to the saturation
concentration at the water temperature and pressure.

The measurement run from 2000 to 2021. We keep stations from the four watershed
(districts) retained for the study. Each measurement keeps:

- **fraction analysed:** raw water, filtered water, sediments...
- **unit:** unit of the measurement value
- **remark code:** indicating for example if the value is below the
quantification limit.

```{r naiades}
naiades <- tar_read(naiades_pc)
naiades_parameter <- tar_read(naiades_parameter)
parameter_name <- setNames(names(naiades_parameter), naiades_parameter)
naiades <- mutate(naiades, parameter = factor(parameter_name[code_parametre], parameter_name))
```

### Coverage

Here is for each parameter: number of measurements, stations, and years covered.

```{r naiades-overview}
naiades |>
  summarise(
    measurements = n(),
    stations = n_distinct(code_station),
    first = min(format(date, "%Y")),
    last = max(format(date, "%Y")),
    .by = parameter
  ) |>
  arrange(parameter) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Fraction analysed

Share of the measurements per fraction analysed. Sediment and other solid
fractions (suspended matter, sediment particles...) are grouped.

```{r naiades-fraction}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

fraction_name <- c(
  "23" = "raw water", "3" = "filtered water", "22" = "unspecified water"
)
naiades |>
  mutate(
    fraction = coalesce(fraction_name[code_fraction], "sediment and other"),
    fraction = factor(fraction, c(fraction_name, "sediment and other"))
  ) |>
  count(parameter, fraction) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = parameter) |>
  ggplot(aes(share, forcats::fct_rev(parameter), fill = fraction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2166AC", "#92C5DE", "grey70", "#B2182B")) +
  labs(x = "Share of the measurements", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Nutrients are mostly measured in filtered water, excepting total phosphorus and
Kjeldahl nitrogen. The rest is mostly measured in raw water. We'll keep only the
main fraction analysed (e.g. filtered water for ammonium) so values are
comparable.

### Units

Units used for each parameter, with their share of the measurements. Units
below 0.1% of the measurements are grouped as "other".

```{r naiades-unit}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

naiades |>
  count(parameter, unit) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = parameter) |>
  mutate(unit = if_else(share < 0.001, "other", unit)) |>
  summarise(share = sum(share), .by = c(parameter, unit)) |>
  mutate(label = reorder(paste(parameter, unit, sep = "__"), share)) |>
  ggplot(aes(share, label)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2166AC", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub(".*__", "", x)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.2), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Share of the measurements", y = NULL)
```

A main unit always dominate, and mg/L is often the second unit which we assume
corresponds to the main one (old notation probably). Measurements with other
units are filtered out.

### Quantification limit

Share of the measurements below the quantification limit (remark code 10). For
these measurements, the value reported is the limit itself. The median limit is
given in the main unit. Temperature and oxygen are left out.

```{r naiades-limit}
main_unit <- naiades |>
  count(parameter, unit) |>
  slice_max(n, by = parameter) |>
  select(parameter, unit)
naiades_limit <- naiades |>
  filter(code_remarque %in% c("2", "7", "10"), parameter %in% parameter_name[1:6]) |>
  semi_join(main_unit, by = c("parameter", "unit")) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")))
naiades |>
  filter(parameter %in% parameter_name[1:6]) |>
  summarise(
    `below quantification (%)` = 100 * mean(code_remarque == "10"),
    `below detection (%)` = 100 * mean(code_remarque == "2"),
    `traces (%)` = 100 * mean(code_remarque == "7"),
    .by = parameter
  ) |>
  left_join(
    naiades_limit |>
      summarise(
        unit = unit[1],
        `median limit` = median(result),
        `2000-2004` = median(result[year <= 2004]),
        `2017-2021` = median(result[year >= 2017]),
        .by = parameter
      ),
    by = "parameter"
  ) |>
  arrange(parameter) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 1, 1, 2, 0, 3, 3, 3))
```

When there is a limit, we set the value to half the limit as it is usually done.

### Sampling frequency

Number of measurements per station and year, for the station-years with at
least one measurement. Station-years with more than 24 measurements are
grouped in the last bar.

```{r naiades-frequency}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

naiades |>
  count(parameter, code_station, year = format(date, "%Y")) |>
  mutate(n = pmin(n, 25)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#2166AC", width = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 6, 12, 24)) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Measurements per station and year", y = "Station-years")
```

We see two peaks at 6 and 12 measurement per year, which means that some
stations have measure every month or every two months. This could be useful to
compute statistics (mean, variance, quantiles).

### Joint measurements

Next, we look at whether parameters are measured independently or jointly.

```{r naiades-joint}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

naiades_sample <- naiades |>
  distinct(code_station, date, parameter) |>
  mutate(present = 1L) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = parameter, values_from = present, values_fill = 0L) |>
  select(all_of(unname(parameter_name)))
joint <- crossprod(as.matrix(naiades_sample))
(joint / diag(joint)) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "parameter") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-parameter, names_to = "parameter_also", values_to = "share") |>
  mutate(across(c(parameter, parameter_also), \(x) factor(x, parameter_name))) |>
  ggplot(aes(parameter_also, forcats::fct_rev(parameter), fill = share)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(100 * share)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Blues", direction = 1, labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0.75, 1), oob = scales::squish
  ) +
  labs(x = "Also measured", y = "Measured", fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

We see that most parameters are measured jointly, and here is below precisely
the share of samples in which all nutrients are measured, and in which all
parameters are measured.

```{r naiades-joint-all}
naiades_sample |>
  mutate(nutrients = rowSums(pick(1:6)), all = rowSums(pick(1:9))) |>
  summarise(
    samples = n(),
    `all nutrients (%)` = 100 * mean(nutrients == 6),
    `all parameters (%)` = 100 * mean(all == 9)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Parameter distributions

Distribution of the quantified measurements after cleaning.

```{r naiades-distribution}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 7

naiades_clean <- tar_read(naiades_clean) |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter_name[code_parametre], parameter_name)) |>
  select(-unit) |>
  left_join(main_unit, by = "parameter")
naiades_clean |>
  filter(!below_limit) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#2166AC", color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ forcats::fct_reorder(paste0(parameter, " (", unit, ")"), as.integer(parameter)), scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of measurements")
```

Spatial distributions of parameter values, averaged over the years.

```{r naiades-value-map}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 13

basin_kept <- tar_read(basin) |>
  filter(district %in% tar_read(params)$district_kept)
station_mean <- naiades_clean |>
  summarise(value = mean(value), n = n(), .by = c(parameter, code_station)) |>
  filter(n >= 12) |>
  inner_join(tar_read(naiades_station), by = "code_station") |>
  sf::st_as_sf()
lapply(parameter_name, \(p) {
  station <- arrange(filter(station_mean, parameter == p), value)
  unit <- main_unit$unit[main_unit$parameter == p]
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = basin_kept, fill = NA, color = "grey40") +
    geom_sf(data = station, aes(color = value), size = 0.4) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(
      name = unit, option = "magma", direction = -1,
      transform = if (p %in% parameter_name[1:6]) "log10" else "identity",
      limits = quantile(station$value, c(0.01, 0.99)), oob = scales::squish
    ) +
    labs(title = p) +
    theme_void()
}) |>
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 3)
```

## Preprocessing the data

From here on, the unit is the station-year: the mean of each parameter per
station and year (log10 for the nutrients). A station-year is kept when each of
the nine parameters has at least 4 measurements spread over at least 3 seasons
(winter December-February, spring, summer, autumn), so that the mean is not
driven by a single season.

### Correlation between parameters

Pearson correlation between the station-year means of the parameters.

```{r naiades-pairs}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

station_year <- tar_read(naiades_station_year)
cor(station_year[unname(parameter_name)]) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "parameter") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-parameter, names_to = "parameter_with", values_to = "correlation") |>
  mutate(across(c(parameter, parameter_with), \(x) factor(x, parameter_name))) |>
  ggplot(aes(parameter_with, forcats::fct_rev(parameter), fill = correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Pearson\ncorrelation") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

### PCA

PCA of the same station-year means, standardised.

```{r naiades-pca}
naiades_pca <- tar_read(water_quality_pca) # PC1 signed to increase with water quality
```

Correlation of each parameter with the first two axes.

```{r naiades-pca-biplot}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7

variance <- 100 * naiades_pca$sdev^2 / sum(naiades_pca$sdev^2)
loading <- cor(station_year[unname(parameter_name)], naiades_pca$x[, 1:2]) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "parameter")
ggplot(loading, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  annotate("path", x = cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)), y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)), color = "grey70") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey80") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), color = "#2166AC"
  ) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = parameter), size = 3.5) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = sprintf("PC1 (%.0f%%)", variance[1]),
    y = sprintf("PC2 (%.0f%%)", variance[2])
  )
```

Station scores on the first two axes, averaged over the years of each station.

```{r naiades-pca-map}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6

station_score <- station_year |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(naiades_pca$x[, 1:2]))
station_score |>
  summarise(across(c(PC1, PC2), mean), .by = code_station) |>
  inner_join(tar_read(naiades_station), by = "code_station") |>
  sf::st_as_sf() |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(PC1, PC2), names_to = "axis", values_to = "score") |>
  arrange(abs(score)) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = basin_kept, fill = NA, color = "grey40") +
  geom_sf(aes(color = score), size = 0.5) +
  scale_color_distiller(palette = "RdBu", limits = c(-4, 4), oob = scales::squish) +
  facet_wrap(~axis) +
  theme_void()
```

Distribution of the station-year scores on PC1 per year (median line and
interquartile band), for all stations and for the stations kept in all 22
years (2000-2021), which show the trend without the change of the station
network.

```{r naiades-pca-year}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

station_full <- station_score |>
  filter(n_distinct(year) == 22, .by = code_station)
bind_rows(
  `all stations` = station_score,
  `stations kept every year` = station_full,
  .id = "stations"
) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(PC1), lower = quantile(PC1, 0.25), upper = quantile(PC1, 0.75),
    .by = c(stations, year)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, median, color = stations, fill = stations)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"), aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PC1 score", color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The rise of PC1 coincides with the fall of the quantification limits around
2010-2013. Setting every nutrient value below the median limit of 2000-2004 to
half this limit, in all years, lowers PC1 after 2012 by only 0.1-0.2, so the
rise is mostly a real improvement of water quality.

## Space-time model of the water quality index (WIP)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Work in progress.** Model fitted and cross-validated (targets
`water_quality_model`, `water_quality_cv`), text and figures to be finished.
:::

PC1 is interpolated in space and time with an INLA model of the station-year
scores:

PC1 ~ intercept + spatial field (SPDE) + year (AR1) + station (iid)

The spatial field is constant over time and the year effect is shared by all
stations. A field changing between years (AR1 on the field) did not fit in
memory. Mesh: edges up to 40 km, nodes at least 15 km apart.

```{r water-quality-model}
tar_read(water_quality_model)$summary.hyperpar[, c("mean", "0.045quant", "0.955quant")] |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

Cross-validation: stations grouped in 50 km blocks, blocks split in 10 folds,
each fold predicted by the model fitted on the others. Coverage is the share of
observations within the 91% predictive interval.

```{r water-quality-cv}
z <- qnorm(0.955)
tar_read(water_quality_cv) |>
  summarise(
    rmse = sqrt(mean((PC1 - mean)^2)),
    `rmse of a constant` = sd(PC1),
    r2 = cor(PC1, mean)^2,
    `coverage 91%` = mean(abs(PC1 - mean) <= z * sd_observation)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

*Where we left (2026-11-10):*

- Full fit: spatial range about 120 km, field SD 1.8, year SD 0.34 (AR1
  correlation 0.84), station SD 1.3, residual SD 0.7.
- Block cross-validation: RMSE 1.57 against 2.14 for a constant, R² 0.47,
  coverage 93%. Error grows with the distance to the nearest training station
  (R² 0.55 under 10 km, 0.14 at 30-50 km).
- 94% of the fish visits (D12) share their Sandre code with a NAIADES station
  that has PC1, and 81% have PC1 measured at that station in the visit year. The
  block cross-validation is therefore pessimistic for our use.
- Next: cross-validation leaving out random station-years (station effect
  known), decide whether to use observed PC1 when available, then predict PC1
  at the fish visits.
